proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathscr X=\sigma(z_0,E_0)\).  By \texttt{def:target} and linearity of conditional expectation,
\[
\tau_n(z_0)
=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{
 n_s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)\mid\mathscr X]
-n_s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(0)\mid\mathscr X]
\right\}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:consistency} gives
\[
n_s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)\mid\mathscr X]
=\mathbb E_P\!\left[n_s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\,middle|\,\mathscr X\right]
=\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0].
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-transport} gives
\[
n_s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(0)\mid\mathscr X]=m_s(z_{0s}).
\]
Substitution proves the identifying equality.  Assumption \texttt{ass:historical-regression} separately establishes that the function appearing on its right-hand side is the observed-law conditional regression learned from the untreated pseudo-event blocks; thus the causal equality is a consequence of consistency and transport, not a definition of the target.

Fix a successful pair \((s,k)\), abbreviate \(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\) by \(\bar B_s\), and let \(\gamma\in\mathbb R^{q_r}\).  The event part of the criterion in \texttt{def:fwl-regression} obeys the exact completion-of-squares identity
\[
\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\theta-e_0^{\top}\gamma)^2
=\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\bar B_s)^2
+(\bar B_s-\theta-e_0^{\top}\gamma)^2.
\]
Consequently, for each fixed \(\gamma\), its unique minimizing event coefficient is
\[
\widehat\theta_{sk}=\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^{\top}\gamma.
\]
At this value the first term is independent of \(\gamma\).  The profiled criterion is therefore, up to the displayed constant,
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}w_{stk}
\{Q_{sti}-b_r(u_{stk})^{\top}\gamma\}^2,
\]
which is exactly the historical weighted least-squares problem in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}.  Passage of the selected Gram-matrix test makes its quadratic form nonsingular, so its minimizer is the selected \(\widehat\gamma_{sk}\).  Hence
\[
\widehat\theta_{sk}=\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^{\top}\widehat\gamma_{sk}.
\]
Finally, using \(\sum_{k=1}^{K_D}K_D^{-1}=1\) and the definitions of \(\widehat m_s\), \(\theta_{\mathrm{FWL}}\), and \(\widehat\tau\),
\[
\theta_{\mathrm{FWL}}
=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s}{K_D}\sum_{k=1}^{K_D}
 (\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^{\top}\widehat\gamma_{sk})
=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat m_s)
=\widehat\tau.
\]

Under the first specialization, \(S=1\) and \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\) imply \(\pi_1=1\).  The identification formula in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and the affine restriction \(m_1(x)=x+\Delta_0\) therefore yield
\[
\tau_n(z_0)
=\mathbb E_P[\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_1(z_{01})
=\mathbb E_P[\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-z_{01}-\Delta_0.
\]
When the proxy is the event cohort's baseline outcome, \(z_{01}\) is its conditional baseline mean; when \(\Delta_0\) is the untreated cohort-average change, the last display is precisely post-event minus baseline for the treated cohort, less the untreated post-minus-baseline change.  This is the canonical conditional finite-cohort two-period difference-in-differences contrast.

For the second specialization define the cohort effect
\[
\tau_s=n_s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)-B_{si}(0)\mid z_0,E_0].
\]
Homogeneity across cohorts says that \(\tau_s=\tau^{\mathrm{com}}\) for every \(s\).  Thus \texttt{def:target} and \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\) give
\[
\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\tau_s
=\tau^{\mathrm{com}}\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
=\tau^{\mathrm{com}}.
\]
The stipulated absence of carry-over beyond \(h=0\) makes this common terminal-level contrast the contemporaneous finite-cohort treatment effect on the buy-and-hold wealth level defined in \texttt{def:buyhold-level}; the algebra does not manufacture that causal interpretation.

Let \(a=2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)\), so \(1-a=d/(2\lambda+d)\).  For every cohort, weighted arithmetic--geometric mean gives
\[
(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
=(n_s^{-1})^a(T^{-2\lambda/d})^{1-a}
\le a n_s^{-1}+(1-a)T^{-2\lambda/d}.
\]
After multiplication by \(\pi_s^2\), summation, and use of \(\sum_s\pi_s^2\le1\),
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\le aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp}}
\le R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}.
\]
Thus the bookkeeping definition alone yields the exact identity
\[
R_\star=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Consequently the algebraic oracle region, generated-proxy region, and boundary are respectively
\[
N^{-\kappa}=o(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}),\qquad
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}=o(N^{-\kappa}),\qquad
N\asymp(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}})^{-1/\kappa}.
\]
Finally, \(\lambda>1\) implies \(\kappa=1\), hence \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-1}\).  Interpreting these algebraic regions as minimax phases still depends on a valid sharp-frontier theorem.
Assumption \texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates} gives \(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\), so the local-polynomial criterion is evaluated at the true historical coordinates and contains no convolution operator to invert.  Inspection of \texttt{def:rate-frontier} then shows that the generated-center contribution is already represented by \(R_{\mathrm{don}}\) and that no additional deconvolution or moving-Gram rate is present.  This establishes the remaining bookkeeping assertions of the narrowed statement.

added_lemmas.statement:
For an admissible fixed choice of class constants with \(H=0\), \(p=S=d=1\), \(\lambda=\kappa=1\), and the uniform order-zero kernel \(K\), there is a triangular array of laws in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\), with \(n_1=N=T^2\), for which
\[
R_\star=T^{-2},\qquad
\lim_{T\to\infty}\mathbb E\!\left[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0\right]=\frac{3}{16}.
\]
In the same array, the event multiplier radius satisfies \(r_{\mathrm{tr}}=0\) almost surely even though the conditional variance of the centered event contribution is \(3/16\).
Moreover, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\),
\[
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
It is enough to exhibit one legal choice of the fixed constants, because the asserted frontier is stated for every law in the displayed class.  Take \(B=16\), \(c_X=C_X=1\), \(c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\), \(\delta_0=1/4\), \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}=C_{\mathrm{mod}}=1\), and \(L\ge1\).  Let \(E_0\) be constant, put \(z_0=1/2\), and take \(\mathcal Z_+=\{1/2\}\).  Let \((X_t)_{t=1}^{T}\) be independent uniform random variables on \([0,1]\).  Set
\[
m(x)=8+x-\frac12,
\qquad
Q_{ti}=m(X_t)+\frac12 U_{ti},
\]
where the \(U_{ti}\) are independent Rademacher variables, independent of the design.  Finally, let the donors be
\[
Z_j=\frac12+V_j,
\]
where the \(V_j\) are independent Rademacher variables independent of all historical variables.

These choices give \(0\le Q_{ti}\le16\),
\(\mathbb E[Q_{ti}\mid X_t,E_0]=m(X_t)\), and
\(\operatorname{Var}(Q_{ti}-m(X_t)\mid X_t,E_0)=1/4\ge B^{-1}\).  The design density is one, and the calendar process is independent over \(t\), hence its conditional beta-mixing coefficients vanish.  Also
\[
\mathbb E[Z_j\mid E_0]=z_0,qquad
\Sigma=1,qquad
\mathbb E[|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)|^4\mid E_0]=1\le B.
\]
Exact training coordinates are obtained by setting \(X_t^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_t\).

For \(0<\delta\le1/4\), the constraint in \texttt{def:local-modulus} is \(|u|\le\delta\), and both \(z_0+u\) and \(z_0-u\) remain in \([0,1]\).  Since \(m(z_0+u)-m(z_0)=u\),
\[
\omega_P(\delta;z_0)=\sup_{|u|\le\delta}|u|=\delta.
\]
Thus both sides of \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus} hold with \(\kappa=1\); the Holder, interior, ellipticity, fourth-moment, and positive-query requirements also hold.

Define \(G=\mathbf 1\{X_1\le1/4\}\) and, for every event unit \(i\), set
\[
B_i(0)=8,qquad B_i(1)=8+G,qquad B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_i(1).
\]
These wealth levels lie in \([0,16]\).  They can be represented by \texttt{def:buyhold-level} by taking \(W_{i,-1}=1\) and \(R_{i0}(a)=B_i(a)-1>-1\).  Set every historical potential outcome equal to the displayed untreated \(Q_{ti}\), independently of its path-status label.  Consistency, historical consistency, limited anticipation, and no spillovers then hold.  Event transport holds because
\[
n_1^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}\mathbb E[B_i(0)\mid z_0,E_0]=8=m(z_0).
\]
Conditional on the complete design path, the event outcomes are constants and the historical error paths are independent across \(i\).  Hence the unit vectors consisting of a historical path and its event outcome are conditionally independent, exactly as required by \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}; within-site replication is immediate.  Donor independence also holds.  This verifies membership in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(1)\).

Because \(G\) is Bernoulli with success probability \(1/4\), \texttt{def:target} gives
\[
\tau_n(z_0)=\mathbb E[B_i(1)-B_i(0)\mid z_0,E_0]=\frac14,
\qquad
\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}=8+G.
\]
We next verify the only estimator fact needed for the counterexample.  For \(n_1=N=T^2\), the initial bandwidth is
\[
h_1=(T^3)^{-1/3}\vee T^{-1}\vee(T^2)^{-1/2}=T^{-1}.
\]
Projection is nonexpansive, so every complementary-fold center is \(1/2+O_{L^2}(T^{-1})\).  Conditional on such a center, the nearest-neighbor distance among \(T\) independent uniform design points is \(O_{L^2}(T^{-1})\).  With \(K(u)=\mathbf 1\{|u|\le1\}\) and \(r=0\), the dyadic selection rule therefore chooses \(h_{1k}=O_{L^2}(T^{-1})\); once one design point enters the window, its \(n_1=T^2\) replicated rows make the scalar Gram matrix exceed the fixed success threshold.  Conditional on the selected design points, the fitted intercept is a convex combination of their within-site averages.  Its squared bias relative to \(m(1/2)\) is \(O(T^{-2})\), while independence of the \(U_{ti}\) gives conditional variance at most \(1/(4n_1)=O(T^{-2})\).  Averaging a fixed number of donor folds preserves this order.  Hence
\[
\widehat m_1-m(1/2)=O_{L^2}(T^{-1}).
\]
The raw estimator consequently satisfies
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=G-\frac14-\{\widehat m_1-m(1/2)\},
\]
and Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
\lim_{T\to\infty}\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
=\mathbb E[(G-1/4)^2]=\frac{3}{16}.
\]
On the other hand, with \(\pi_1=1\), \(n_1=N=T^2\), and \(\lambda=d=\kappa=1\),
\[
R_{\mathrm{tr}}=T^{-2},\quad
R_{\mathrm{sm}}=(T^3)^{-2/3}=T^{-2},\quad
R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2},\quad
R_{\mathrm{don}}=T^{-2},
\]
so \(R_\star=T^{-2}\).  Finally all event observations equal \(8+G\), whence
\[
E_{1i}=n_1^{-1}(B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}})=0
\]
for every \(i\).  Therefore \(G_{\mathrm{tr}}^{\#}=0\) and \(r_{\mathrm{tr}}=0\), although \(\operatorname{Var}(G-1/4\mid E_0)=3/16\).  The witness isolates the missing conditional-mean stability: conditioning on the full design makes the units independent but does not make their event means stable after the design is integrated out.

It remains to verify the asserted failure of the reported interval.  The retained set has cardinality of order \(T\).  Uniformly over the full fit and the \(M=O(T^{2/3})\) delete-one-block fits, a union bound for uniform nearest-neighbor spacings gives selected bandwidth
\[
O_P\!\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right).
\]
For any selected local-constant fit, conditional on its design and donor center, its noise is a convex combination of within-site averages of \(n_1=T^2\) independent Rademacher variables scaled by \(1/2\).  The elementary inequality \(\cosh(x)\le e^{x^2/2}\), applied to the conditional moment-generating function, makes this noise sub-Gaussian with variance proxy at most \(1/(4n_1)\).  A union bound over the \(M+1\) fits therefore shows that the maximum fitted-noise magnitude is
\[
O_P\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{n_1}}\right)
=O_P\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{\log(T\vee2)}}{T}\right).
\]
Thus the maximum difference between the full retained fit and any delete-block fit is \(O_P(\log(T\vee2)/T)\).  Since \(M=O(T^{2/3})\), the definitions of \(J_b\) and \(C_b\) imply
\[
\max_{b\le M}|C_b|=O_P\!\left(\frac{M\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right)=o_P(1).
\]
For every multiplier realization,
\[
|G_{\mathrm{cal}}^{\#}|
\le\{M(M-1)\}^{-1/2}\sum_{b=1}^{M}|C_b|
\le\sqrt{\frac{M}{M-1}}\max_{b\le M}|C_b|,
\]
so \(r_{\mathrm{cal}}=o_P(1)\).  For the order-zero fit, successful local-constant weights are nonnegative and sum to one.  Consequently the deterministic Taylor allowance satisfies
\[
A_L=O_P\!\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right),
\]
and the donor formula with \(m_k\asymp N=T^2\) gives \(A_{\mathrm{don}}=O(T^{-1})\).  All declared bad-sample conditions are absent with probability tending to one: \(M\ge3\) and \(m_k\ge1\) eventually, the scalar Gram search succeeds by bandwidth one for every full and delete-block fit, every constructed quantity is finite, spectral clipping is defined, and \(\max_k\delta_k\le\delta_0\) eventually.  Hence
\[
H_\alpha=o_P(1),qquad \widehat\tau_R\longrightarrow G
\quad\text{in probability}.
\]
Because \(|G-1/4|\ge1/4\) almost surely, the interval coverage tends to zero.  This proves that the frozen honest-interval claim, not merely its proposed proof route, fails on the declared class.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For each of the treated-mean, replicated-smoothing, random-spacing, and covariance-aligned donor channels, there are pairs \((P_{0,q},P_{1,q})\subset\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\), with \(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{don}\}\), such that \(P_{\ell,q}(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\mid E_0)\ge c_X\), their joint observed-data testing affinity is uniformly bounded away from zero,
\[
\inf_{N,T,\mathbf n}\int\min\{dP_{0,q},dP_{1,q}\}>0,
\]
and \(|\tau_{n,P_{1,q}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,q}}(z_0)|^2\ge cR_q\) on \(\mathcal Z_+\).  The treated-mean, replicated-smoothing, and donor pairs may additionally be chosen to have uniformly bounded Kullback--Leibler divergence; only testing affinity, rather than bounded Kullback--Leibler divergence, is asserted for the random-spacing pair.  Every pair is induced by a regular conditional law of the complete causal panel rather than by a labeled fixed-query kernel.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The random-spacing experiment is separated by the positive probability that no design point falls in the local bump. With replicated responses, the usual bump pair has Kullback--Leibler divergence of order \(n_sT^{-2\lambda/d}\), which is unbounded in allowed growth regimes. A uniform lower bound on testing affinity is the correct and sufficient Le Cam premise; bounded Kullback--Leibler divergence remains available for the other three channels.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Define the restricted class
\[
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)
=\left\{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda):
P\text{ satisfies \texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability} and
\texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering}}\right\}.
\]
There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on fixed class constants, such that along every array with \(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\), uniformly for \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\) and \(P\)-almost every \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\),
\[
cR_\star
\le\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le CR_\star.
\]
The raw feasible estimator in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator} attains the upper bound with nonidentically distributed bounded event outcomes, an unknown heteroskedastic donor law, and estimated full \(\Sigma\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen class permits design-measurable conditional event means and historical errors shared by every replicate. The explicit obstruction shows that the risk of the advertised estimator then stays bounded away from zero while the four-term frontier vanishes. Restricting to full-design event-mean stability and historical centering removes exactly those extra common-noise channels without assuming the desired rate conclusion.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Uniformly over fixed \(S\),
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}\le R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}},
\qquad
R_\star=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Consequently, in any experiment for which \(R_\star\) is established as the sharp risk, the oracle region is \(N^{-\kappa}=o(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}})\), the generated-proxy region is \(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}=o(N^{-\kappa})\), and the boundary is \(N\asymp(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}})^{-1/\kappa}\).  Assumption \texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates} means that the historical design enters the estimator without a measurement-error inverse problem, so the core's rate bookkeeping contains neither a deconvolution term nor a separate moving-Gram term.  Finally, \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-1}\) whenever \(\lambda>1\).  This algebraic statement does not by itself assert sharpness over the unrepaired original panel-law class.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The algebraic rate diagram is valid, but its unconditional minimax interpretation inherits the sharp-frontier theorem that the counterexample invalidates on the frozen class. The proposed claim preserves the exact domination, boundary, saturation, and absence of a training-coordinate deconvolution term while making the sharp-risk interpretation explicitly conditional on a valid frontier.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Define \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\ddagger}(\lambda)\) as the subclass of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\) satisfying \texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability}, \texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering}, and \texttt{ass:event-conditional-variance}.  Along arrays for which
\[
N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\longrightarrow\infty,
\qquad
\frac{\min_s T h_s^d}{\log(T\vee2)}\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
the interval \(C_\alpha\) in \texttt{def:honest-interval} satisfies
\[
\liminf\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\ddagger}(\lambda)}
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}\ge1-\alpha,
\qquad
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\ddagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]\le C R_\star^{1/2}.
\]
Every interval with the same uniform conditional coverage has worst-case conditional expected length at least \(cR_\star^{1/2}\).  In this dense-local-design regime the retained-block coupling error obeys \(M\beta_0\rho_0^{g_T}=o(1)\), the block jackknife/Rademacher law consistently estimates the calendar fluctuation, and the event Rademacher law consistently estimates the bounded conditionally independent triangular-array fluctuation.  The donor fourth-moment calibration and the deterministic Holder-bias allowance remain as in \texttt{def:honest-interval}.  No assertion is made that the displayed block jackknife remains honest when \(T h_s^d=O(1)\); that spacing regime requires an additional within-site calibration or a different interval construction.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The displayed multiplier interval is not uniformly honest under the current sampling assumptions. Conditional independence given the full design permits a common random event mean, and when the number of local calendar sites stays bounded the delete-block statistic has only finitely many influential pseudo-scores. The proposed claim adds the missing mean and variance conditions and restricts this particular block multiplier to the dense-local-design regime; the spacing regime needs a different within-site calibration.

proposed_assumptions.condition:
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\,middle|\,(X_{s't'})_{1\le s'\le S,\,1\le t'\le T},E_0\right]
=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]
\quad\text{for every }s,i.
\]
proposed_assumptions.reason: Conditional independence after conditioning on the complete historical design does not eliminate covariance created by design-dependent conditional event means. This condition removes that shared component while retaining nonidentically distributed bounded outcomes.

Centering only on the contemporaneous coordinate permits every replicate to share a design-measurable omitted component. Full-design centering makes the existing conditional cross-unit independence deliver the advertised replication gain.

proposed_assumptions.condition:
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\,middle|\,(X_{s't'})_{1\le s'\le S,\,1\le t'\le T},E_0\right)\ge B^{-1}
\quad\text{for every }s,i.
\]
proposed_assumptions.reason: The unstudentized event Rademacher quantile can be identically zero for a degenerate or rare triangular-array component. A uniform conditional variance lower bound supplies the Lindeberg and scale stability needed by the retained event multiplier construction.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}\), estimated by the raw \(\widehat\tau\); the \(R_\star\) sharp-risk guarantee is asserted only on the subclass satisfying \texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability} and \texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering}, and remains to be proved after those assumptions and the affinity-corrected lower-bound embedding are applied.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The frozen functional line advertises a sharp risk equality over the original class, but the counterexample disproves that guarantee. The identifying functional is unchanged; only the class qualification on the estimator guarantee is corrected.

In this dense-local-design regime the retained-block coupling error obeys \(M\beta_0\rho_0^{g_T}=o(1)\), the block jackknife/Rademacher law consistently estimates the calendar fluctuation, and the event Rademacher law consistently estimates the bounded conditionally independent triangular-array fluctuation.  The donor fourth-moment calibration and the deterministic Holder-bias allowance remain as in \texttt{def:honest-interval}.  No assertion is made that the displayed block jackknife remains honest when \(T h_s^d=O(1)\); that spacing regime requires an additional within-site calibration or a different interval construction.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A sharp upper frontier can only be proved after the event full-design mean-stability and historical full-design centering assumptions are adjudicated and incorporated into the panel-law class; the matching converse also awaits the affinity-corrected embedding.
open_obligations.obstruction: The theorem is false on the frozen class. Conditional cross-unit independence given all historical coordinates permits a shared design-measurable event component that replication does not average away.
open_obligations.attempted: The event and historical variance decompositions were carried out before applying local-polynomial bounds. They expose surviving covariance of conditional means, and an explicit admissible triangular array makes the feasible estimator's conditional risk stay bounded away from zero while the proposed frontier vanishes.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The present class does not admit the asserted upper bound.  The explicit legal array in \texttt{prop:shared-design-replication-obstruction} has
\[
R_\star=T^{-2}
\quad\text{but}\quad
\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]\longrightarrow\frac{3}{16}.
\]
The variance decomposition identifies the missing term: for event units,
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}},B_{si'}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0)
=\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(
\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0],
\mathbb E[B_{si'}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
\,middle|\,E_0\right)
\]
for \(i\ne i'\), where \(\mathscr X\) is the full historical design, because conditional independence only removes the conditional covariance.  The proposed full-design mean-stability condition sets this surviving covariance to zero.  The analogous full-design centering condition is needed for replicated historical errors to gain the factor \(n_s^{-1}\).

proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(a=a_{\mathrm w}\).  We first exhibit a common completion of the variables left unspecified by \texttt{def:mean-only-witness}.  Conditional on a fixed event state \(E_0\), take the realized center to be the displayed \(z_0\).  For each calendar window let \(X_{1t}\) be uniform on \([0,1]^d\), independently over \(t\).  Given \(X_{1t}=x\), draw the sign pairs independently over \((t,i)\) with
\[
 P_\rho(U_{1ti}=u,V_{1ti}=v\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
 =\frac{1+\rho(x)uv}{4}.
\]
Because \(|\rho(x)|\le1-2\delta_0\), each displayed probability is at least \(\delta_0/2>0\), and summing over \((u,v)\in\{-1,1\}^2\) gives one.  Draw the event-date sign pairs independently over \(i\), conditionally on \((z_0,E_0)\), from the analogous law with \(x=z_0\).  Set
\[
 B_{1i}(0)=(1+aU_{1i})(1+aV_{1i}),
 \qquad B_{1i}(1)=B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=1,
\]
and set \(Q_{1ti}(0)=Q_{1ti}(1)=Q_{1ti}\), where
\[
 Q_{1ti}=(1+aU_{1ti})(1+aV_{1ti}).
\]
These assignments give consistency, historical consistency, no spillovers, and limited anticipation as stated in \texttt{ass:consistency}, \texttt{ass:historical-consistency}, \texttt{ass:no-spillovers}, and \texttt{ass:limited-anticipation}.

For the donor sample, let \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\) be conditionally independent and uniform on the Euclidean sphere of radius \(\sqrt d\) in \(\mathbb R^d\), independently of all historical and event outcomes, and put
\[
 Z_j=z_0+\xi_j.
\]
Rotational invariance gives \(\mathbb E[\xi_j\mid E_0]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[\xi_j\xi_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_d\).  Hence the center and covariance in the frozen definitions are indeed
\[
 \mathbb E[Z_j\mid E_0]=z_0,
 \qquad \Sigma=I_d.
\]
Since \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\), donor ellipticity holds.  Moreover,
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[
   \left\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\right\|_2^4
   \mathrel{\big|}E_0
 \right]
 =\mathbb E[\|\xi_j\|_2^4\mid E_0]=d^2\le B.
\]
Thus donor replication, donor independence, ellipticity, and the fourth-moment condition all hold.  This also verifies that the full, rather than coordinatewise, covariance is used.

We next compute the historical conditional law.  Directly from the four sign probabilities,
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_\rho}[U_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0]
 =\mathbb E_{P_\rho}[V_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0]=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{P_\rho}[U_{1ti}V_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0]=\rho(x).
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 m_1^{P_\rho}(x)
 &=\mathbb E_{P_\rho}[(1+aU_{1ti})(1+aV_{1ti})mid X_{1t}=x,E_0]\\
 &=1+a\mathbb E[U_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0]
   +a\mathbb E[V_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0]
   +a^2\mathbb E[U_{1ti}V_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0]\\
 &=1+a^2\rho(x).
 \end{aligned}
\]
This proves the historical regression restriction.  The added compatibility condition places this surface in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\).  Its range is admissible because
\[
 0<(1-a)^2\le Q_{1ti}\le(1+a)^2<4\le d^2\le B,
\]
where \(d=2p\ge2\).  The same inequalities give \(0<B_{1i}(0)\le B\), while \(B_{1i}(1)=1\le B\).  Thus both bounded-wealth restrictions hold.

For completeness, the conditional response variance is not being hidden in the construction.  Since
\[
 Q_{1ti}=1+a(U_{1ti}+V_{1ti})+a^2U_{1ti}V_{1ti},
\]
the identities \((U+V)^2=2+2UV\) and \((U+V)UV=U+V\) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}_{P_\rho}(Q_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
 &=2a^2\{1+\rho(x)\}+a^4\{1-\rho(x)^2\}\\
 &\ge B^{-1}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The inequality is exactly the displayed response-variance compatibility condition in the statement.  Because \(\varepsilon_{1ti}=Q_{1ti}-m_1(X_{1t})\), it proves \texttt{ass:response-variance}.

The uniform design has density one, so \(c_X\le1\le C_X\) proves \texttt{ass:design-density}.  Conditional independence of the sign pairs over \((t,i)\) gives within-site replication and cross-unit independence.  The calendar process is conditionally independent over \(t\), hence its absolute-regularity coefficients satisfy \(\beta_{P_\rho}(k\mid E_0)=0\) for every \(k\ge1\), which implies \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}.  Define \(X_{1t}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{1t}\) to obtain exact training coordinates.  The choice of \(z_0\) gives the interior condition, and the degenerate event-state completion gives
\[
 P_\rho\{z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\}=1\ge c_X.
\]
Finally, the definition of \(\mathcal R\) states that the induced surface \(1+a^2\rho\) obeys the two-sided local-modulus inequalities.  All member properties in \texttt{def:panel-law-class} have therefore been verified, so \(P_\rho\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(\lambda)\) for every \(\rho\in\mathcal R\).  The parameter family is relatively open because its index set \(\mathcal R\) is relatively open by definition.

The event-date untreated signs have the same conditional calculation, so
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_\rho}[B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]=1+a^2\rho(z_0)=m_1^{P_\rho}(z_0).
\]
This verifies event transport.  Since \(S=1\) forces \(\pi_1=1\), the causal target in \texttt{def:target} is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \tau_{n,P_\rho}(z_0)
 &=n_1^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
   \mathbb E_{P_\rho}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]\\
 &=1-\{1+a^2\rho(z_0)\}=-a^2\rho(z_0).
 \end{aligned}
\]
This derives the causal contrast from the potential outcomes and event transport; it does not define that contrast by the observed regression.

It remains to establish observational equivalence for the restricted information map.  Summing the sign-pair law over the other sign gives
\[
 P_\rho(U=u\mid x,E_0)=P_\rho(V=v\mid x,E_0)=\frac12.
\]
Thus every untreated return coordinate has the same symmetric two-point marginal on \(\{-a,a\}\) and mean zero for every \(\rho\); every treated return coordinate is identically zero.  Also \(W_{1i,-1}=1\) and \(B_{1i}(1)=1\) under every law.  By \texttt{def:mean-only-information}, it follows that
\[
 \mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_\rho)
\]
is constant in \(\rho\).

To find two separated laws, choose any \(\rho_*\in\mathcal R\).  Relative openness supplies an \(\epsilon>0\) such that every member of the Holder ball within Holder-norm distance \(\epsilon\) of \(\rho_*\) belongs to \(\mathcal R\).  Choose a constant function \(c\) in that ball with \(c\ne\rho_*(z_0)\), and for \(0<\eta<1\) put
\[
 \rho_\eta=(1-\eta)\rho_*+\eta c.
\]
Convexity of the Holder ball puts \(\rho_\eta\) in the ball, while
\[
 \|\rho_\eta-\rho_*\|_{\mathcal H_d}
 =\eta\|c-\rho_*\|_{\mathcal H_d}<\epsilon
\]
for sufficiently small \(\eta\).  Hence \(\rho_\eta\in\mathcal R\), and
\[
 \rho_\eta(z_0)-\rho_*(z_0)
 =\eta\{c-\rho_*(z_0)\}\ne0.
\]
Taking \(\rho^{(0)}=\rho_*\) and \(\rho^{(1)}=\rho_\eta\), the restricted information maps agree, but the already derived target formula gives
\[
 \left|\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(1)}}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(0)}}}(z_0)\right|
 =a^2\left|\rho^{(1)}(z_0)-\rho^{(0)}(z_0)\right|>0.
\]
Equal values of \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}\) therefore do not determine \(\tau_n\).  The joint sign law, and hence generally the distribution of the compounded historical wealth \(Q_{1ti}\), changes with \(\rho\); accordingly the argument establishes no equivalence under the full historical wealth panel.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Consider the one-cohort, two-return specialization \(S=1\) and \(H=1\), so that \(d=2p\), and fix
\[
 z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\cap[\delta_0,1-\delta_0]^d.
\]
Suppose, in addition to \(0<a_{\mathrm w}<1\), that
\[
 B\ge d^2,\qquad
 \inf_{\rho\in\mathcal R}\inf_{x\in[0,1]^d}
 \left[2a_{\mathrm w}^2\{1+\rho(x)\}
       +a_{\mathrm w}^4\{1-\rho(x)^2\}\right]\ge B^{-1},
 \qquad
 \{1+a_{\mathrm w}^2\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}
 \subset\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L).
\]
Then the construction in \texttt{def:mean-only-witness} has a common completion for which the \(\rho\)-indexed, relatively open family
\[
 \{P_\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}
 \subset\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(\lambda).
\]
For every \(\rho\in\mathcal R\) and \(x\in[0,1]^d\), the untreated return-coordinate means are zero and their conditional coordinate marginals do not depend on \(\rho\), whereas
\[
 m_1^{P_\rho}(x)
 =\mathbb E_{P_\rho}[Q_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0]
 =1+a_{\mathrm w}^2\rho(x),
 \qquad
 \tau_{n,P_\rho}(z_0)=-a_{\mathrm w}^2\rho(z_0).
\]
There consequently exist \(\rho^{(0)},\rho^{(1)}\in\mathcal R\) such that \(\rho^{(0)}(z_0)\ne\rho^{(1)}(z_0)\),
\[
 \mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho^{(0)}})
 =\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho^{(1)}}),
 \qquad
 \left|\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(1)}}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(0)}}}(z_0)\right|
 =a_{\mathrm w}^2\left|\rho^{(1)}(z_0)-\rho^{(0)}(z_0)\right|>0.
\]
Thus \(\tau_n\) is not a functional of \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}\) on this submodel. This conclusion concerns only mean-only return-path matching; it does not assert observational equivalence under the full historical wealth panel.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen claim is not valid uniformly over its stated constants or dimensions. The witness definition fixes one cohort and two return horizons, while an unrestricted amplitude need not satisfy the maintained bounded-wealth and conditional-variance restrictions. The narrowed statement exposes sufficient support, variance, smoothness, query-region, and dimension conditions without assuming the nonidentification conclusion.

proposed.justification: The result isolates the information loss from discarding within-path dependence without denying identification from the maintained full wealth panel.
proposed.gap: Barber--Lyon and Goldsmith-Pinkham--Lyu diagnose volatility drag; this proposition gives an explicit two-law, relatively open nonidentification result for the restricted mean-only map while preserving the possibility of full-panel identification under event transport.
proposed.consumer: Analysts can determine whether a return-matching procedure discards dependence information needed for a finite-cohort compounded-wealth effect.
